#Converting Categorical Variables into Factors
```{r}
categorical_variables <- c(
  "School",
  "Gender",
  "Residence",
  "Family_Size",
  "Parent_Status",
  "Mother_Occupation",
  "Father_Occupation",
  "School_Choice_Reason",
  "Guardian",
  "School_Support",
  "Family_Support",
  "Paid_Classes",
  "Extracurricular_Activities",
  "Nursery_Attendance",
  "Higher_Education_Intent",
  "Internet_Access",
  "Romantic_Relationship"
)

student[categorical_variables] <- lapply(
  student[categorical_variables],
  factor
)

str(student)
```
# Checking Missing Values
```{r}
# Count missing values in each variable
colSums(is.na(student))

# Calculate the total number of missing values
sum(is.na(student))
student_clean <- na.omit(student)
```
#3. Simple Linear Regression
```{r}
simple_model <- lm(
  Final_Grade ~ Study_Time,
  data = student_clean
)

summary(simple_model)
```

```{r}
plot(
  student_clean$Study_Time,
  student_clean$Final_Grade,
  main = "Relationship Between Study Time and Final Grades",
  xlab = "Study Time",
  ylab = "Final Grade",
  pch = 19
)

abline(simple_model, lwd = 2)
```
#Multiple Linear Regression
```{r}
multiple_model <- lm(
  Final_Grade ~ Age +
    Mother_Education +
    Father_Education +
    Study_Time +
    Past_Failures +
    School_Absences +
    Social_Outings +
    Health_Status +
    Gender +
    Internet_Access,
  data = student_clean
)

summary(multiple_model)
```
#Polynomial Regression
```{r}
polynomial_model <- lm(
  Final_Grade ~ Age + I(Age^2),
  data = student_clean
)

summary(polynomial_model)
```
# Building the Interaction Model
```{r}
interaction_model <- lm(
  Final_Grade ~ Study_Time * Past_Failures +
    Age +
    School_Absences +
    Gender,
  data = student_clean
)

summary(interaction_model)
```
